Committee: Economic Development and Tourism
Sponsor: Rafferty
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 02/07/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 234 as introduced would increase the administrative obligations of the Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board to require the board to establish and issue licenses to food trucks in Class 1 municipalities to sell alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption. This increase in obligations could by offset, wholly or in part, by certain license fees collected and retained by the board. This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund up to $150 for each food truck license fee collected due to the provisions of this bill, in addition to any other applicable application or renewal fee.
Andy Whitt, Chair
Economic Development and Tourism

Committee: Tourism
Sponsor: Rafferty
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver
Date: 03/29/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 234 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the administrative obligations of the Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board to require the board to establish and issue licenses to food trucks in Class 1 municipalities to sell alcoholic beverages for on-premises consumption in an established entertainment district. This increase in obligations could by offset, wholly or in part, by certain license fees collected and retained by the board. This bill could also increase receipts to the State General Fund up to $300 for each food truck license fee collected due to the provisions of this bill, in addition to any other applicable application or renewal fee.
Del Marsh, Chairperson
Tourism
